summary: This is a carefully executed, fully preregistered paired emulation study of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline. Execution, logging, and archival are comprehensive and the authors correctly report a degenerate null outcome (no discordant pairs) driven by the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics. The work is reproducible given the archived artifacts and includes the mandatory master-prompt locator + SHA‑256. However, the manuscript requires a small set of resolvable revisions before finalisation: principally IEEE‑style reference formatting and an explicit, prominent Methods/Results disclosure that the primary confirmatory inference was untestable because the baseline unsafe rate was zero (degenerate paired test). Also require explicit runtime-sampling disclosure (temperature unset) and clarification of determinism implications under shared_initial_candidate semantics.
critical_issues: References are supplied as raw arXiv/DOI identifiers rather than a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full metadata; this violates the track requirement and prevents standard citation semantics verification.

The preregistered primary confirmatory test (H1) is effectively untestable because baseline unsafe rate = 0 (n11=240, n10=n01=0). The manuscript mentions this in Discussion, but it must prominently state in Methods and Results that the confirmatory inference is degenerate and interpretive consequences for H1 (i.e., the registered inferential test cannot provide evidence for or against verifier benefit under the executed semantics).

Runtime sampling semantics are underspecified in the manuscript: model_configuration.json records temperature = null. The paper must explicitly state that temperature was unset, that shared_initial_candidate semantics were used, and that unset temperature does not imply deterministic sampling; discuss the implication for generator variability and the paired contrast.

References in prose must use numbered IEEE citation markers and every cited record must be verified to support the proximate scholarly claim (current cited_record_ids must be converted to full IEEE entries).
required_revisions: Replace the References section with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (full author/title/venue/year metadata) and convert all in-text citations to numeric IEEE markers; verify each cited record supports the nearby claim and correct any mismatches from the archived evidence bundle.

In Methods and Results (not only in Discussion), add an explicit, prominent statement that the primary confirmatory hypothesis (H1) could not be tested as planned because the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0 (n11=240, no discordant pairs), explain how this makes the McNemar/bootstrap inference degenerate, and state the limited inferential scope of the completed confirmatory analysis.

Explicitly disclose runtime-sampling semantics: report that model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (unset) and explain that shared_initial_candidate semantics were used so one initial generation was reused across paired arms; clearly state that unset temperature does not imply deterministic sampling and describe the potential impact on generator variability and the estimand.

Update the Disclosure Statement to remain concise while keeping the mandatory providence pair (provenance/master_prompt.txt and its SHA‑256) exactly as required; do not replicate detailed per-call logs in the manuscript body (refer readers to the archived manifest), and confirm the Disclosure remains within pages 1–5.
optional_revisions: Add a short, evidence‑anchored speculation in Results/Discussion about why the baseline unsafe rate was zero (e.g., task-generator conservatism, verifier permissiveness, adversary strength) with pointers to representative artifacts; label this explicitly exploratory.

Add a short, specific plan for a follow‑up confirmatory run (within the archived artifacts) that varies generation semantics (independent initial generation or larger repair budget) and/or increases adversary adaptivity; this can be framed as concrete future work rather than new experiments.

Tighten figure captions to note that zero repair invocations and zero unsafe applies are a product of the shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, to avoid potential misreading that the verifier is universally redundant.
